title: Risk-aware negative budgets and calibrated weighting for KGE
setting: A synthetic typed knowledge graph (80 entities, 4 relations, cluster-compatibility rules plus latent affinities and heterogeneous entity popularity) is the closed world. Each true triple is observed with probability p to form the open-world training KG, and unobserved true triples form the test set. TransE or DistMult (dim 16) is trained with a logistic contrastive loss using a fixed total negative budget of K per positive; the metric is filtered MRR on held-out true triples (head and tail prediction), and the fraction of sampled negatives that are actually true in the closed world is reported as a diagnostic.

paper.title: How Many and How Much? Contrastive Learning with Negative Samples for Knowledge Graph Embedding
paper.claim: Allocating negatives per positive by estimated false-negative risk (observed anchor degree) and weighting negatives by score dispersion and concentration (RADAR) improves link-prediction quality and cuts sampled false negatives versus fixed-budget uniform negative sampling.

metric.name: mrr
metric.description: Filtered mean reciprocal rank (head and tail queries, filtered against the closed-world truth) of held-out true triples that were unobserved during training. Diagnostics: hits10, fn_rate (fraction of sampled valid negatives that are true in the closed world), neg_used_per_pos, n_train.

factors.name: method
factors.description: uniform: fixed K negatives per positive with unit weights. radar: degree-based risk-aware budget allocation (same total budget) plus distribution-calibrated negative weighting.

factors.name: p
factors.description: Observation probability of closed-world triples; low p means a sparse KG with many unobserved true triples (more false negatives).

factors.name: K
factors.description: Average number of negatives per positive (total budget = K times the number of training positives).
